spec.summary:
Since `201` a video project is made of tracks, but it still has exactly one video track: a single picture at any
moment, with text and stickers on top. Creators of Reels, Shorts and YouTube videos routinely need a second picture
over the first: B-roll cut over someone talking (the sound of the main clip continues), a face-cam in a corner of a
screen recording, a product shot beside a review, a logo clip over the intro. This feature lets the user add
**overlay tracks** above the main video track, put video and photo clips on them at any time, and place each overlay
clip in the frame with a **position, size, rotation and opacity** (picture-in-picture), or leave it covering the
whole frame (B-roll). Every frame draws every visible clip at that time, bottom track first, and the preview and the
exported MP4 match. Projects with no overlay clips look, sound and export exactly as they do after `201` and `202`.
It needs the decoder pool (`204`) to decode several videos at the same moment.

US-1.text: As a vlogger, I want to cut B-roll over my talking clip while my voice keeps playing, so that the video isn't one long shot of my face.

US-2.text: As a creator of tutorials and reactions, I want a small clip (my face, a product) in a corner of the main clip, so that viewers see both at once.

US-3.text: As a video creator, I want to move, resize, rotate and fade an overlay clip directly on the preview and with exact numbers, so that I can place it where I want.

US-4.text: As a keyboard or screen reader user, I want to add tracks and place overlay clips without a mouse, so that I can do everything anyone else can.

US-5.text: As a creator with an older 2.x or `201` / `202` project, I want it to play and export exactly as before, so that the update costs me nothing.

US-6.text: As a contributor building `205`–`212`, I want one tested model of tracks drawn in order with a transform per clip, so that keyframes (`205`), transitions (`206`) and agent tools (`212`) animate and reach the same properties.

AC-1.text: The user can add an **overlay** track (Q12), rename it, move it up or down among the overlay tracks and delete it (with its clips, after a confirmation if it holds any). The main video track is always the bottom picture track (Q10). Video and overlay tracks together are limited to 4 on the web and 8 on the desktop app (the limits of `201` Q4); at the limit **Add track** is disabled and says why. Each of these is one undo step.

AC-2.text: An overlay track's header has **Hide** (picture not drawn in the preview or the export), **Mute** (its clips' sound silent in the preview and the export, Q7), **Lock** (as in `201` AC-10, including on the preview: a locked overlay clip can't be moved, resized or selected for editing there) and the height menu.

AC-3.text: Video and photo files can be added to an overlay track at the playhead (button, and by dropping files onto the track; dropping onto the empty area above the top track creates a new overlay track, Q12). Clips can be dragged in time on their track and between picture tracks (main ↔ overlay), with the clip keeping its start time unless snapping moves it. `202`'s operations (trim, ripple trim and delete, roll, slip, slide, split, duplicate, snapping) work on overlay tracks, which are never magnetic (Q8): clips there never overlap and gaps are allowed.

AC-4.text: Each clip on a picture track has a **transform**: position (the clip's centre as a share of the frame, from −0.5 to 1.5 on each axis so a clip can sit partly outside), size (its width as a share of the frame width, 0.05 to 4), rotation (−180° to 180°) and opacity (0–100 %), with Q2's corner radius. The clip keeps its own aspect ratio inside its box. A new overlay clip starts full frame (B-roll) (Q4); the inspector offers **Full frame** and the four **corner** presets (35 % of the frame width, 4 % margin). Main-track clips start and stay at the identity transform unless the user changes it.

AC-5.text: On the preview, a selected overlay clip shows a box with handles: drag to move, corner handles to resize keeping the aspect ratio, a rotate handle; moves snap to the frame's centre lines and edges within 8 px (off with the Snap switch or Alt, as `202` Q4). The inspector has number fields for X, Y, size, rotation, opacity and corner radius. With an overlay clip selected and the preview focused, arrow keys move it by 1 % of the frame (10 % with Shift). A drag is one undo step however long; each change is announced to screen readers (the clip and its new values).

AC-6.text: At every frame time `t`, the frame is: the main video track's clip at `t` (black in a gap or past its end), then each visible overlay track's clip at `t` from the lowest track to the highest, each with its transform and opacity, then the timed layers on top of all tracks (Q1). Gaps on an overlay track draw nothing (the tracks below show through). Golden frames: a fixture with the main track and 2 overlay tracks (a full-frame B-roll video, a corner face-cam video with 50 % opacity, a rotated photo with rounded corners, a clip partly outside the frame), at 9:16 and 16:9, at 8 sample times including each clip's first and last frame, matches its reference within the self-test's tolerance on every GPU backend, and the export renders the same frames from the same inputs.

AC-7.text: Timing is frame-exact: an overlay clip starting at 2.0 s at 30 fps appears first in frame 60 and is gone in the frame after its last; hidden tracks and clips at 0 % opacity draw nothing; a full-frame opaque overlay clip covers the frame completely (no pixel of the main clip shows).

AC-8.text: Sound: each overlay video clip's own sound plays at its clip volume, mixed with the main track's clips and the music, in the preview and the export; a muted overlay track adds nothing. The export's sound sources (start, end, source time, volume, ramps) for a fixture with overlays equal the expected list exactly.

AC-9.text: The video's length is the end of the last clip on any picture track (Q9); the per-platform length and clip limits (`limitsFor()`) apply to the whole project, counting clips on every track (Q6), and refusals use the existing messages. At most Q6's number of video clips are visible at the same moment; an edit that would exceed it is refused with a message that says the limit and why.

AC-10.text: Projects with no overlay clips (`201`'s fixtures: photo-only, video-only, mixed, music with offset, timed layers, fade-out, at 9:16, 4:5, 1:1 and 16:9; and `202`'s with gaps) give pixel-identical preview frames at 10 sample times each and identical export inputs (frames, clips, times and sound sources) to `202`. All existing video e2e tests pass unchanged.

AC-11.text: The project document reads every existing document unchanged (Q11): the new fields are optional and their defaults are the identity transform and no overlay clips. The validator clamps out-of-range transform values, drops clips on a missing track with a reason, moves a clip that overlaps another on an overlay track to the end of the one it overlaps (as `202` D3, never dropping it), enforces the track and clip limits, and never throws: at least 30 new malformed documents. Round trips document → validator → document are equal for the AC-6 fixture.

AC-12.text: Preview: with the main track and 2 overlay tracks each playing a 1080p 30 fps video at the same moment (a 1080 × 1920 Reel and a 1920 × 1080 YouTube project), the median preview frame time over 300 frames is ≤ 33 ms in the desktop app and, with main + 1 overlay, ≤ 33 ms in Chrome on the development machine (Q13). A project without overlays stays within 5 % of `202` (fastest of 3 runs, as `201` AC-5).

AC-13.text: Exporting a 2-minute 1080p fixture with main + 2 overlay video tracks completes on desktop and web and leaves no open `VideoFrame` (the check `204` adds), and its export time is recorded in the plan's measurements.

AC-14.text: Adding, renaming, reordering, hiding, muting, locking and deleting tracks, adding overlay clips and setting every transform value work from the keyboard alone with labelled controls; axe reports no serious or critical issue on the timeline and the inspector; at 360 px wide everything works with no sideways scroll; the preview handles respect `prefers-reduced-motion` (no animated outlines).

AC-15.text: `docs/MEDIA-STUDIO.md` (overlay tracks, picture-in-picture, presets, keys, limits), `specs/lld.md` (the drawing order, the transform, the document fields) and `CHANGELOG.md` describe the change; the in-app docs list the keys.

Q1.text: `201` Q2 and `202` Q6 left to 203 whether the timed layers (text, shapes, stickers, drawings, images) move onto overlay tracks. _Answer (accepted 2026-10-09):_ not in 203. Layers keep their own start / end and are drawn above every track, as today; ripples don't move them. Putting layers in the track stack (a title under a PiP clip) is reconsidered with compound clips and groups (`210`).

Q2.text: Which properties does a clip's transform have? _Answer (accepted 2026-10-09):_ position, uniform size, rotation, opacity and a **corner radius** (0–50 % of the box's shorter side), the common picture-in-picture look. No crop, border, shadow or non-uniform stretch in 203; the clip keeps its aspect ratio. Today's per-clip framing (fill / whole picture with blurred background, zoom, position inside the frame) keeps working inside the box.

Q3.text: Can main-track clips be transformed too (e.g. shrink the main clip over a coloured or black background)? _Answer (accepted 2026-10-09):_ yes, the same transform on every picture track (one model, and `205` animates it the same way); main-track clips default to full frame, and the area they leave uncovered is black.

Q4.text: Where does a new overlay clip appear? _Answer (accepted 2026-10-09):_ full frame (B-roll, the most common use), with **Full frame** and four corner presets in the inspector (35 % of the frame width, 4 % margin from the edges, on the safe side of the platform's UI for Reels / Shorts).

Q5.text: Blend modes on overlay clips (screen, multiply … as photo layers have)? _Answer (accepted 2026-10-09):_ not in 203: normal only. They are cheap to add later on the same drawing path and can come with a Phase 3 item.

Q6.text: Limits. _Answer (accepted 2026-10-09):_ the per-platform clip limits (20 / 50 / 60 / 500) count clips on every track; at most **3** video clips visible at the same moment on the web and **6** on the desktop app (photos don't count), the final numbers set from `204`'s measurements before 203's plan is approved.

Q7.text: Sound of overlay clips. _Answer (accepted 2026-10-09):_ an overlay video clip's own sound plays at its clip volume (B-roll often has ambient sound the user can lower); overlay tracks get both **Hide** and **Mute** in their header (`201`'s Hide on the main track hides pictures only, D2, and stays so).

Q8.text: How do overlay tracks behave with Magnetic and ripples? _Answer (accepted 2026-10-09):_ overlay tracks are never magnetic (free placement, gaps allowed, no overlaps); a ripple on the main track moves only main-track clips, as in `202` Q6. Connected clips that follow the main track can come later.

Q9.text: What sets the video's length when an overlay clip ends after the main track? _Answer (accepted 2026-10-09):_ the last clip end on any picture track; after the main track ends, its area is black under the overlays. The music and layers keep their own times.

Q10.text: Track order. _Answer (accepted 2026-10-09):_ the main video track stays the bottom picture track and can't be moved or deleted; overlay tracks are listed above it in drawing order and moved with up / down buttons in their header (keyboard-friendly, like `201` Q5's height menu), each an undo step.

Q11.text: Project document version. _Answer (accepted 2026-10-09):_ stays **1**: overlay tracks already exist in the v1 model (`201` AC-1) and the transform is a new optional field with identity defaults, as `202` added Magnetic (`202` Q1). Bump to 2 only if the plan finds a change an old reader would misread.

Q12.text: How is a track added? _Answer (accepted 2026-10-09):_ an **Add track** button under the track headers (adds an empty overlay track at the top), and dropping files on the empty area above the top track creates one with the files placed at the drop time. New tracks are named "Overlay 1", "Overlay 2" …

Q13.text: Performance target. The Phase 2 gate is a 4K timeline with 3 video and 2 audio tracks playing smoothly on desktop, which also depends on proxies (`211`). _Answer (accepted 2026-10-09):_ 203 proves 1080p (AC-12); the 4K gate is measured at the end of Phase 2, after `211`.

Q14.text: Constitution XI (agent tools). _Answer (accepted 2026-10-09):_ as in `201` Q7 and `202` Q7, no tools in 203; tracks, overlay clips and transforms are plain operations on the project so `212` (which needs 203) exposes them. The gap stays recorded.

changelog.text: Q1–Q14 resolved (all proposals accepted by the maintainer); Approved.
Q6's limits set from 204's measurements (AC-15): 3 videos at once on the web, 5 on the desktop app (not the proposed 6). Plan drafted (§1–§14, D1–D3 for the maintainer).

sections.title: Non-Functional Requirements
sections.markdown:
- Performance: AC-12, AC-13; drawing a frame with no overlay clip costs no more than in `202`.
- Memory: at most Q6's number of videos decoded at once; frames are released as soon as they are drawn (`204`).
  Photos on overlay tracks follow today's per-photo memory budget (docs/PERFORMANCE.md).
- Accessibility: AC-14 (WCAG 2.2 AA in light and dark themes, keyboard, screen reader, 360 px).
- Compatibility: web and desktop alike, with fewer tracks on the web (AC-1, Q6) for memory reasons only
  (Constitution V); Firefox and Safari get the same result through the existing Canvas 2D / WebGL2 paths.
- What you see is what you get: one drawing path for preview and export (Constitution VIII); no export-only
  compositing.
- Security: project data only enters through the validator (AC-11).
- Licences: no new library, model or asset.

sections.title: Out of Scope
sections.markdown:
- Keyframed (animated) position, size, rotation and opacity (`205`); transitions between clips (`206`); speed
  (`207`); audio-only tracks beyond the music (`208`).
- Blend modes on clips (photo layers have them; Q5), crop of overlay clips, borders and shadows (Q2), chroma key and
  background removal for overlays.
- Clips connected to a main-track clip so they move with it in a ripple (Final Cut's connected clips; Q8).
- Moving the timed layers (text, stickers, drawings) onto tracks (Q1).
- Compound clips and groups (`210`); proxies (`211`).
- Agent tools for tracks and overlay clips (`212`; Q14).
- Saving and opening video projects as files (`201` Q1).

AC-10 regressions while the main row, the stage frame and the export loop are rewritten. → Identity fast path; the testkit oracles (`videoAt`, `framePlan`, `audioPlan` of 201 / 202) compared on every fixture before any UI work; all existing video e2e tests run unchanged after each UI task.

Memory: the stage pool at videosAtOnce + 2 decoders (7 on desktop) with 4K sources: 5 × 4K × 5 frames ≈ 830 MB, under the 1 GB budget; `makeRoom` drops read-ahead first (204). → AC-13 records peak bytes; 4K proxies are `211`.

sections.title: Approach
sections.markdown:
What the code is today (read for this plan on `main` after 204, `5ff8fab`):

- **Model** (`engine/timeline.ts`): tracks of kind video / overlay / audio already exist (201); only `V1` (main video)
  and `A1` (music) are ever made. `videoAt(p, t)` returns the single topmost visible clip; `framePlan` walks the main
  track's clips; `audioPlan` mixes main-track clip sound and the music. `patchTrack` lets only audio tracks mute.
- **Drawing** (`engine/video.ts`): `renderFrame` fills black, draws one clip with `renderIg` into the whole frame
  (its framing: fill / whole picture, zoom, position; a photo's motion), the layers, then the darkness of the clip's
  fade-in and the video's fade-out.
- **Edits** (`engine/edits.ts`, 202): pure, per track; Magnetic packs only the main track (`pack`).
- **Preview** (`previewFrame.ts`, `VideoStage`): one shown clip and one picture; the pool (204) with
  `poolLimits(1)`; `lanePlan` already plans every visible picture track. Sound: `previewSound.ts`, one current clip.
- **Export** (`videoExport.ts`): `framePlan` spans, one clip at a time through the export's pool.
- **Timeline** (`Timeline.tsx`): rows hard-wired as main video, layers, music; `TrackHead` has Hide or Mute, Lock and
  the height menu.
- **Limits**: `limitsFor().videosAtOnce` is 3 on the web and 5 on the desktop app (1 without `VideoDecoder`), set by
  204's measurements by Q2 / Q6's rule (Q6's "6 on the desktop app" was a proposal; 204 measured 5).

**§1 The clip transform (engine/timeline.ts, AC-4).** Every picture clip may carry `tf?: ClipTransform` = `{ x, y, w,
rot, opacity, radius }`: the box's centre as a share of the frame (−0.5…1.5), its width as a share of the frame width
(0.05…4), rotation in degrees (−180…180), opacity (0…1) and corner radius (0…0.5 of the box's shorter side, Q2). The
names and meanings are the layers' (`engine/layers.ts`: x, y, w, rot, opacity), so the stage reuses the layers' box
geometry and handles. Missing = `IDENTITY` (`{0.5, 0.5, 1, 0, 1, 0}`). The box has the frame's aspect ratio (D1): at
identity it is the frame, so a clip without a transform draws exactly as today, and the clip's own framing (fill /
whole picture with blurred background, zoom, position) works inside the box unchanged; nothing is ever stretched.
`clampTransform` clamps every field; `PRESETS` = Full frame and the four corners (w 0.35, 4 % margin of the frame
width from the two nearest edges, Q4). A new overlay clip gets no `tf` (full frame); main-track clips likewise.

**§2 Tracks (engine/timeline.ts, AC-1, AC-2).** Pure functions on the track list, each returning the new list or a
reason: `addTrack(tracks, desktop)` (an empty overlay track at the top, named "Overlay N" with the lowest free N, Q12;
refused at `TRACK_LIMITS` with the message the button shows), `renameTrack` (1–40 characters), `moveTrack(id, ±1)`
(only among overlay tracks: the main track stays the bottom picture track, Q10), `deleteTrack(tracks, clips, id)`
(overlay only, with its clips). `patchTrack` lets overlay tracks mute too (Q7); the main track keeps Hide only (201 D2).
Track order in `tracks` is drawing order (bottom first), as today.

**§3 What shows at a time (engine/timeline.ts, AC-6, AC-7, AC-9).** `frameStack(p, t)` is the picture clips drawn at
`t`, bottom to top: the visible main track's clip at `t`, then each visible overlay track's clip at `t`. The main
track keeps `videoAt`'s clamp only where 201 / 202 had it (before 0; at or past the **video's** end its last clip), so
after the main track ends but before an overlay clip does, its area is black (Q9). Frame-exactness is `frameRange`'s
(a clip starting at 2.0 s first shows in frame 60). `videoAt` stays (the topmost item of the stack) for its callers.
`mostVideosAt(clips, tracks)` is the most video clips on screen at once (a sweep over clip intervals on every picture
track, hidden tracks included so unhiding can't break the limit, D3); photos don't count.

**§4 Drawing (engine/video.ts, AC-6, AC-7, AC-10).** `renderStack(ctx, W, H, items, layers, t, total, fadeOut)`, items
= `{ clip, src, sw, sh, local }[]` bottom first: black; each item with its picture; the layers; the darkness. An item
at identity draws through exactly today's call (`renderIg(ctx, src, sw, sh, edit, W, H)`), so a project without
transforms is pixel-identical (AC-10). Otherwise `save`, `globalAlpha = opacity`, `translate(x·W, y·H)`, `rotate`,
`scale(w)`, `translate(−W/2, −H/2)`, a rounded-rectangle clip (`roundRect`, `arcTo` where missing), `renderIg(…, W, H)`,
`restore`. Fades (D2): the main track clip's fade-in darkens the whole frame as today (layers included, 2.x's look);
an overlay clip's fade-in ramps its own opacity from 0 over `V_FADE`; the video's fade-out darkens everything as
today. `renderFrame` becomes `renderStack` with one item (its callers unchanged until §5 / §6 move them).

**§5 Preview (previewFrame.ts, VideoWorkspace.tsx).** `StageFrame` carries `items: { clip, local, pic }[]` instead of
one `shown` / `pic`. `pausedAt` / `pausedFrame` use `frameStack` on the export's grid and resolve every item's
picture together (photos' stills at once, videos from the pool, latest wins per lane). Playing, each tick `peek`s
every visible video (holds counted per lane as in 204). `drawPreview` calls `renderStack`. The stage's pool becomes
`poolLimits(limitsFor().videosAtOnce)` (decoders = limit + 2; the byte budget unchanged: 3 × 1080p × 5 frames ≈
124 MB of 256 MB). The paused "held picture" is kept per clip, so an overlay arriving doesn't blank the main clip.

**§6 Export (videoExport.ts, AC-6, AC-10, AC-13).** The frame loop walks frames 0…N and draws `frameStack(p, i / fps)`:
videos through the export's pool (`poolLimits(videosAtOnce)`, `maxWidth` as 204 D5), every visible video's frame
awaited together; photos decoded once per clip and released after its last frame; `want` = `lanePlan(t, 2)` (visible
and next), `prepare` for the next, `forget` once a clip has passed. A video's last frame is held past a short
source's end, per clip, as today. `framePlan` stays (tests, and AC-10's oracle: the new loop's (frame, clip, source
time) list for a project without overlays must equal what `framePlan` gives).

**§7 Sound (timeline.ts audioPlan, previewSound.ts, AC-8).** `audioPlan` adds each video clip of an overlay track that
isn't muted (hidden keeps the sound: Hide is pictures, Q7) with the same 0.03 s ramps as main-track clips; the main
track's entries and their order don't change (AC-10's identical sound sources). `soundPlan` returns `current` as a
list (every clip sounding at `t`: the main clip and each unmuted overlay clip) and `previewSound` keeps one element per
current clip; D1's bound becomes current + next + covered, still bounded by the visible-video limit.

**§8 Limits and edits (engine/edits.ts, state/video.ts, AC-3, AC-9).** `EditCtx` gains `maxVideos`; the store's
`apply` refuses an edit whose result has `mostVideosAt > maxVideos` (and more than before) with "At most N videos can
show at the same time here (the desktop app allows M)": the message names the limit and why (memory and decoding).
New pure edit `moveToTrack(clips, id, track, start, ctx)`: onto an overlay track as `moveTo` places (nearest free
spot, never overlapping); onto the main track with Magnetic on, inserted at its time's index and packed; locks checked
on both tracks. Overlay tracks are never packed (`pack` already touches only the main track, Q8). Every 202 operation
already works per track. Clip limits count every track's clips (already `state.clips.length`); the length is
`projectLength` (already every picture track, Q9).

**§9 Store actions (state/video.ts).** `addTrack`, `renameTrack`, `moveTrack`, `deleteTrack`, `setTrack` (Mute for
overlays), `addMedia(files, { track?, at? })` (overlay: at the playhead or the drop time, after the clips already there
if it doesn't fit; dropping above the top track first adds a track), `moveClipToTrack`, `setClipTransform(id, patch,
key)` (one undo step per drag via the 800 ms key coalescing), `applyPreset(id, preset)`. Each is one undo step.

**§10 Timeline UI (Timeline.tsx, AC-1–AC-3, AC-14).** The main row's clip rendering, trims, tools and drags move into a
`PictureRow` used for every picture track; rows are listed top track first (overlays above the main track), then the
layers and music rows as today. `TrackHead` for overlays: the name as a button that turns into a text field (Enter /
Escape), ↑ / ↓ buttons, Delete (a confirmation when it holds clips), Hide, Mute, Lock and the height menu. **Add track**
sits under the track headers (disabled with the reason at the limit). A clip dragged up or down onto another picture
row moves there (`moveClipToTrack`); files dropped on a row land at the drop time, above the top row in a new track.
Keyboard: the clip menu gets "Move to track…" (the picture tracks), so nothing needs a mouse.

**§11 Stage UI (VideoWorkspace.tsx, new `studio/useClipTransform.ts`, AC-5, AC-14).** A selected overlay clip (or a
main clip with a transform) shows its box with the layers' handles (`drawSelection`, `handleAt`, `rotationFor` from
`engine/layers.ts`). Layers are drawn on top, so a press goes to a layer first, then to the selected clip's box.
Move snaps the box's centre and edges to the frame's centre lines and edges within 8 screen px (`snapBox`, pure,
in engine/timeline.ts; off with the Snap switch or Alt as 202 Q4); corner handles resize keeping the aspect; the rotate
handle turns (Shift: 15° steps). Arrow keys with the stage focused move it 1 % (Shift 10 %). Each change is announced
in 202's live region ("Overlay 1 clip: x 72 %, y 20 %, size 35 %"). The inspector (ClipPanel) gets a **Position and
size** group: Full frame and the four corner presets, number fields for X, Y, size, rotation, opacity and corner
radius. Locked tracks: no box, fields disabled with the reason. Reduced motion: no animated outlines.

**§12 Project document (engine/timeline.ts, AC-11).** `DocClip.transform?: ClipTransform`, written by `toDocument` only
when not identity (so 201 / 202 documents round-trip byte-identical); `mergeProject` clamps it, keeps overlay tracks
and their clips, and the overlap rule of 202 D3 applies to every picture track (`unpacked` generalised: a clip that
overlaps another on its track moves to that clip's end, never dropped). Version stays 1 (Q11): a 2.10 reader drops the
unknown `transform` field and shows overlay clips full frame, a degraded but not misread picture.

**§13 Measurements (AC-12, AC-13).** `playbackChecks` gains the AC-12 timing (main + 2 overlay 1080p30 videos, Reel
and YouTube projects, 300 frames, median and p95; and a no-overlay project against `main`, fastest of 3) in
`CHITTHI_TEST_ONLY=pooltiming`; the Chrome figure (main + 1) is a manual run (`?selftest&only=pooltiming`). AC-13's
2-minute export with main + 2 overlays runs in the self-test with `openFrames()` 0 after it and its time recorded.

**§14 Agent tools.** None in 203 (Q14): tracks, overlay clips and transforms are plain store actions and pure functions,
which `212` exposes. Constitution XI's gap stays recorded.

sections.title: Data Structures & Interfaces
Techniques
sections.markdown:
- **Canvas transforms around the existing draw.** `renderIg` draws into the context it is given at (0, 0, W, H), so
  the transform is a `save` / `translate` / `rotate` / `scale` / clip / `restore` around today's call: no second
  renderer, one path for preview and export (Constitution VIII). Whether the whole-picture framing's blurred
  background (a canvas `filter`) and the GPU-drawn looks behave under a transformed, clipped context is checked first
  (spike T001).
- **Identity is a fast path, not a special case of maths.** An item without `tf` (or at identity) calls exactly
  today's code, so AC-10's pixel equality is structural, then proven on 201's fixtures.
- **`roundRect`** (Chromium 99, Safari 16, Firefox 112) with an `arcTo` path where missing; radius 0 skips the clip.
- **A sweep for the videos-at-once limit:** sort the video clips' start / end events, count, keep the maximum (O(n log
  n), cheap at 500 clips); run on every edit's result.
- **Reuse the layers' geometry** (`Box`, `handleAt`, `rotationFor`, `drawSelection`) so overlay boxes handle like
  layers; snapping is a pure function so it is unit-tested.
- **Every visible video awaited together** in the export (`Promise.all` on the pool's lanes), so two videos decode in
  parallel; the pool's latest-wins and byte budget hold as in 204.
- **Performance:** one extra `save`/`restore` and clip per overlay item; a project with no overlays runs the same code
  as today (AC-12's 5 % check).

sections.title: Decisions for the maintainer (accepted 2026-10-11: D1–D3 as recommended)
sections.markdown:
- **D1 — The box's shape.** _Recommended:_ the box has the **frame's** aspect ratio; the clip's own framing (fill,
  or whole picture with blurred background) decides what shows inside, as it does today for the full frame. Identity =
  today's look (AC-10 by construction), one model for main and overlay clips. _Alternative:_ the box takes the clip's
  own aspect (a 16:9 face-cam in a 9:16 Reel is a 16:9 box, nothing cropped), but Full frame then needs its own fill
  rule and main clips change model. With D1, a 16:9 face-cam in a corner shows cropped until its framing is set to
  "whole picture"; the corner preset could set that for videos whose aspect differs from the frame's.
- **D2 — Fade-in on an overlay clip.** _Recommended:_ it fades the clip in (opacity 0 → its opacity over 0.5 s); the
  main clip's fade-in keeps darkening the whole frame from black as today.
- **D3 — What the videos-at-once limit counts.** _Recommended:_ video clips on every picture track, hidden tracks
  included, so unhiding a track can never exceed it; photos don't count (Q6).
- **Q6's number.** The desktop limit is **5** (204's measurement by Q2's rule), not the proposed 6; the web stays 3.
